---
title: "Error messages, decoded"
subtitle: "What Git and GitHub are actually telling you"
---

Git's error messages are written for people who already understand Git. This
page translates the ones you are most likely to meet, roughly in the order
people meet them.

**Find your error by its text.** Use Ctrl/Cmd+F on this page and search for a
distinctive phrase from the message you got.

## Quick index

| The message you saw | Jump to |
|---|---|
| `could not find function "gph_..."` | [The course commands are not loaded](#not-loaded) |
| `git: command not found` | [Git is not installed](#git-not-found) |
| No Git tab in RStudio | [No Git tab](#no-git-tab) |
| `Please tell me who you are` | [Git does not know your name](#who-are-you) |
| `Authentication failed`, `Invalid username or password` | [Password rejected](#auth-failed) |
| `Support for password authentication was removed` | [Password rejected](#auth-failed) |
| `remote: Repository not found` | [Repository not found](#repo-not-found) |
| `Updates were rejected` | [Push rejected](#rejected) |
| `Your local changes would be overwritten by merge` | [Pull blocked by local edits](#pull-blocked) |
| `<<<<<<< HEAD` inside a file | [Merge conflict](#conflict) |
| `fatal: not a git repository` | [Not a repository](#not-a-repo) |
| `Permission denied (publickey)` | [SSH key problem](#publickey) |
| `does not exist` from `create_from_github()` | [Destination folder missing](#destdir) |
| `this exceeds GitHub's file size limit` | [File too large](#too-large) |
| `You are in detached HEAD state` | [Detached HEAD](#detached-head) |
| `Everything up-to-date` but GitHub looks empty | [Pushing the wrong branch](#wrong-branch) |

## The course commands are not loaded {#not-loaded}

**You see:**

```
> gph_inclass()
Error in gph_inclass() : could not find function "gph_inclass"
```

**What it means:** the course helper commands are not loaded in this R session.
They are not part of R, so every new session starts without them. Restarting
R, opening a different project, or reopening RStudio all give you a fresh
session.

**Fix:** run this, then try your command again.

```r
source("https://gph-2182.github.io/gph2182.R")
```

You will know it worked when `gph_start`, `gph_check` and the others appear
under **Functions** in the Environment pane.

**Permanent fix:** run `gph_autoload()` once. It saves a copy in your home
folder and loads it at every startup, so you never type the `source()` line
again. Undo it with `gph_autoload(remove = TRUE)`.

---

## Git is not installed, or RStudio cannot find it {#git-not-found}

**You see:** `git: command not found`, or `bash: git: No such file or directory`,
or RStudio's **Tools > Global Options > Git/SVN** box is empty.

**What it means:** Git is a separate program from R and RStudio, and either it
was never installed or RStudio has not noticed it.

**Fix:**

- macOS: run `xcode-select --install` in the RStudio Terminal tab.
- Windows: install Git for Windows from
  [git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win), accepting all
  defaults.
- Then **restart RStudio**. It only looks for Git at startup, so a running
  RStudio will not see a fresh installation.

If Git is installed but the Git/SVN box is still empty, type the path in
yourself: `/usr/bin/git` on macOS, `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/git.exe` on
Windows. Then restart RStudio.

Full instructions: [Installing R, RStudio, and Git](install.qmd).

---

## There is no Git tab in RStudio {#no-git-tab}

**You see:** the top-right pane shows Environment, History, and Connections, but
no Git.

**What it means:** almost always that you opened a plain folder or a loose file
rather than an RStudio project that is also a Git repository.

**Fix, in order of likelihood:**

1. Check the **top-right corner** of the window. If it says "Project: (None)",
   you do not have a project open. Open the `.Rproj` file in the folder, or use
   **File > Recent Projects**.
2. If you downloaded the repository as a ZIP from GitHub, that copy is not a
   repository at all: the Git history is not included in a ZIP. Delete it and
   clone properly, per [guide 3](rstudio-projects.qmd).
3. If the project is open and it really was cloned, check **Tools > Global
   Options > Git/SVN** and confirm **Enable version control interface** is
   ticked and the Git path is filled in. Restart RStudio afterward.

---

## Git does not know your name {#who-are-you}

**You see:**

```
*** Please tell me who you are.
Run
  git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
  git config --global user.name "Your Name"
```

**What it means:** Git stamps every commit with an author and refuses to commit
without one.

**Fix:** in the RStudio Console:

```r
usethis::use_git_config(
  user.name  = "Your Name",
  user.email = "you@example.edu"
)
```

Use the email on your GitHub account, so your commits are credited to your
profile. Then commit again.

---

## Your password is rejected {#auth-failed}

**You see:** `Authentication failed`, `Invalid username or password`,
`fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/...'`, or
`remote: Support for password authentication was removed on August 13, 2021`.

**What it means:** GitHub does not accept account passwords for Git operations.
It needs a personal access token. If RStudio is prompting you for a password at
all, no token is stored.

**Fix:**

```r
usethis::create_github_token()   # opens GitHub; set Expiration to a date you choose
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()         # paste the token here
usethis::git_sitrep()            # confirm it is stored
```

If this used to work and just stopped, your old token expired. The fix is the
same: generate a new one and store it with `gitcreds_set()`, choosing
**replace** when it offers the menu.

Full walkthrough: [Connecting RStudio to GitHub](github-setup.qmd).

---

## Repository not found {#repo-not-found}

**You see:** `remote: Repository not found`, or `fatal: repository
'https://github.com/...' not found`.

**What it means:** GitHub is saying "either that repository does not exist, or
you are not allowed to see it". It gives the same message for both, on purpose,
so that private repository names cannot be probed.

**Check, in order:**

1. **Typo in the URL.** Owner and repository name are both case-sensitive in
   practice. Copy the URL from your browser rather than retyping it.
2. **You are not signed in as the right account.** Run
   `usethis::git_sitrep()` and look at the GitHub user it reports. A stored
   token for a personal account cannot see a private organization repository.
3. **You do not have access yet.** If it is private and belongs to someone else,
   you need to be added as a collaborator or organization member.

::: {.callout-tip}
## In this course

This usually means you have not accepted the GitHub organization invitation
that was emailed to you, or it expired after seven days. Ask for a fresh
invitation, accept it, then try again.
:::

## Updates were rejected {#rejected}

**You see:**

```
! [rejected]  main -> main (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do
      not have locally.
```

**What it means:** GitHub has commits that your computer does not. Git refuses
to push, because doing so would erase them. This is Git protecting you.

**Fix:** click **Pull**, then **Push**. That downloads the missing commits and
merges them with yours.

This happens most often when you edited a file directly on github.com in the
browser, or worked from a second computer. If the pull produces a conflict, see
[merge conflict](#conflict) below.

---

## Pull blocked by local changes {#pull-blocked}

**You see:** `error: Your local changes to the following files would be
overwritten by merge` followed by a file name.

**What it means:** you have uncommitted edits to a file that the incoming
commits also change. Git will not silently discard your edits.

**Fix:** commit your edits first, then pull.

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Work in progress"
git pull
```

Committing is the right move even if the work is unfinished. A commit is a
private checkpoint, not a publication, and you can always tidy the history
later.

---

## Merge conflict {#conflict}

**You see:** markers like these inside one of your files, and Git reports
`CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in exercise.qmd`.

```
<<<<<<< HEAD
mean_age <- mean(df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
=======
mean_age <- mean(df$age)
>>>>>>> origin/main
```

**What it means:** two commits changed the same lines and Git will not guess
which one wins. The text between `<<<<<<< HEAD` and `=======` is yours; the text
between `=======` and `>>>>>>>` is the incoming version.

**Fix:** open the file, decide what the lines should say (possibly a blend of
both), delete all three marker lines, save, then stage and commit. That commit
is the resolution.

Nothing is broken while a conflict is open, and nothing is lost. Take your time.

---

## Not a git repository {#not-a-repo}

**You see:** `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories):
.git`.

**What it means:** you are running a Git command in a folder that Git does not
manage.

**Fix:** you are probably in the wrong directory. Check with `getwd()` in the
Console, and open the right project. If this folder genuinely should be a
repository, make it one with `usethis::use_git()`.

---

## Permission denied (publickey) {#publickey}

**You see:** `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey). fatal: Could not
read from remote repository.`

**What it means:** the repository's remote URL uses SSH (`git@github.com:...`),
but GitHub does not have an SSH key that matches yours.

**Fix, the simple way:** switch that repository to HTTPS, which uses the token
you already have.

```bash
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/owner/repository-name.git
```

**Fix, the other way:** set up an SSH key, as described in the
[Happy Git with R SSH chapter](https://happygitwithr.com/ssh-keys).

---

## create_from_github() says the folder does not exist {#destdir}

**You see:** an error from `usethis::create_from_github()` complaining that the
`destdir` path does not exist or is not a directory.

**What it means:** `create_from_github()` will not create the parent folder for
you; it requires it to be there already.

**Fix:** create it first, in the same block:

```r
dir.create("~/gph2182", showWarnings = FALSE)
usethis::create_from_github("owner/repository-name", destdir = "~/gph2182")
```

`showWarnings = FALSE` makes the first line harmless when the folder already
exists.

---

## File too large {#too-large}

**You see:** `remote: error: File data/big.csv is 214.00 MB; this exceeds
GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB`.

**What it means:** GitHub refuses individual files over 100 MB, and warns above
50 MB. The whole push fails, not just that file.

**Fix:** stop tracking the file, and ignore it going forward.

```bash
git rm --cached data/big.csv
```

```r
usethis::use_git_ignore("data/big.csv")
```

Then commit and push again. Note that if the large file is already in an earlier
commit, removing it now is not enough: the history still contains it, and
cleaning that up is a bigger job. It is far easier to keep large data out of Git
from the start, and to store it elsewhere with a script that downloads it.

---

## You are in detached HEAD state {#detached-head}

**You see:** `You are in 'detached HEAD' state`, usually after clicking around
in the History view.

**What it means:** you are looking at an old commit rather than at the tip of a
branch. It is a viewing mode, not damage. Commits made here can be hard to find
later.

**Fix:** go back to your branch.

```bash
git checkout main
```

If you made commits while detached and want to keep them, `git switch -c
rescue-branch` before checking out `main`, and ask for help merging them.

---

## Push succeeds but GitHub looks unchanged {#wrong-branch}

**You see:** `Everything up-to-date`, or a successful push, but the repository
page on github.com does not show your work.

**Check three things:**

1. **Which branch you are on.** The Git tab shows it at the top right of the
   pane. If you are on a branch other than `main`, your commits went there;
   GitHub's repository page shows `main` by default. Use the branch dropdown on
   GitHub to look, then merge or open a pull request.
2. **Which repository you are looking at.** Confusing a fork, a template, and
   your own copy is easy. Run `git remote -v` and compare it against the URL in
   your browser.
3. **Whether you actually committed.** `Everything up-to-date` means there were
   no new commits to send. Saved but uncommitted files are still only on your
   disk. Check the Git tab: any files still listed are not committed.

---

## Still stuck?

Before asking anyone, collect these three things. With them, almost any question
gets answered in one reply; without them, the answer is always "what does the
error say?".

1. **The exact error text**, copied as text or a screenshot. Not a paraphrase:
   the specific words are what identify the problem.
2. **The output of `usethis::git_sitrep()`**, which shows your Git identity,
   your token, and the repository's remote in one block. It contains no
   secrets, so it is safe to share.
3. **What you did immediately before**, in one sentence.

Pasting all three into an AI assistant resolves most setup problems in a couple
of turns. If it does not, bring the same three things to office hours or an
email.
